criteria.name: artwork_craft
criteria.why: Frames 1, 7 and 9 are a place at an hour. There's a storm deck, cured grass, a caprock in haze and a pad with contact under the mast, and on frame 9 the pipe gate and caliche road with its wheel tracks are the best-built passage in the deck. Too many frames fall short of that. Frame 2's 'pole top a reader knows' is a flat untextured cylinder with stacked brown discs for insulators and a hard black cone at the crossarm end. It stands over a flat ground plane with sparse sprite grass, and the top conductor runs to within a few pixels of the 'o' in the hook's 'to'. Frame 8 is rows of chairs floating on tile in a black void, with no dais and no walls. The hook and dek sit on a visibly edged rectangle, top edge at about y230 and right edge at about x1460 at display size, which reads as a type plate. That is the defect round 1 named, now dark instead of lit. On frame 6 the caprock ends in a clean artificial curve at the left third with a pale band under it, which is a render artifact behind the 33 heads. Frame 3's caprock is a smeared low-res texture wall that reads as near, not 4 km out, and machine_qa warns its three labels are 22px, under the 24px floor. Frame 9's rancher is a low-poly kit figure. Frames 4 and 5 are a competent but generic desk interior, and the 'window' reads as a monitor. On the descriptors this is several frames leaning on primitives, not one, so it sits under 7.

criteria.name: deck_coherence
criteria.why: The contact sheet reads as one deck. It holds one stormFront world, dark sky tops with the type in the same quiet, and one station hero in one galvanized-and-white-powder-coat material on frames 1, 3, 6, 7 and 9. The caliche road leaves frame 1 bottom right and arrives at the gate on frame 9, and it works as an edge tease. The camera moves around one station and the heads motif changes state (splayed on 1, close on 3, 33 on the rail on 6, facing the lens on 9). Three frames sit outside the outdoor world, the desk on 4 and 5 and the hearing room on 8. The storyboard declares frame 8 as the value cut, but it also reads as a different piece of stock (blue chairs, void, plate). Frame 2's station on the ridge, which the storyboard promises, doesn't read at feed size, so the hero is effectively absent there too.

criteria.name: claim_integrity
criteria.why: I checked every slide string and the caption against claims.json. Every numeral traces to a quote: 33 and 34 for 2026 (c8), July 10th, 2025 (c10, c31), May 1st (c9), $10,537,400, $6,423,554 and 64.04% (c15), 24 (c18), 26 (c20), 2027 (c57), eight and 160 (c43), Dockets 57463 and 57941 (c10, c9). The absence on frame 6 is scoped to 'that line', and 'A missing count isn't a count of none' blocks the zero misreading. The caption fairly credits what the report does count (24 ignitions, 26 wildfires) and its partial-year caveat (c21). Nothing is Colorado and 97 appears nowhere. Every frame 3 label is a verbatim substring. Deductions: the Smokehouse Creek cause (frame 2) and 'Eight of 160' (frame 8) rest on the Tribune, where the hearing record and investigative reports exist. Frame 8's 'lists cameras as a "Suggested" tool' compresses c37, where the Suggested marking is on section 4.5 Situational Awareness and cameras are one tool listed inside it. Frame 9's 'Under the order that report carries the same detections line' states a future report's contents in the present tense on the strength of FoF 51 (c34). It's defensible but a notch firmer than the source. The first comment lists six sources and every one is a fetched claim URL.

criteria.name: story_and_stakes
criteria.why: Reading it once in the feed, a Texan learns what happened (the PUCT order asked for a count of AI camera fire detections and SPS's May 1st report answered with 33 cameras). They learn who decided (the PUCT, Docket 57463), where (the Panhandle) and why it bites: frame 2 ties it to Smokehouse Creek, and frame 7 shows the camera budget up to $10,537,400. What the deck doesn't give is anything to DO. Frame 9 offers two docket numbers to look up and 'its 2027 annual report', with no date, although c6 and c58 carry the May 1 deadline. There is no county, although c54 (Moore) and c55 (Hutchinson) are in the claims file, and there's no proceeding a reader can enter. The storyboard's own job for frame 9 is 'the one formal way in', and the frame no longer delivers it. Its fence still carries 30 T-posts driven by intervene_days, a figure no surface now states. Frame 8 also never tells the reader that the wildfire mitigation plan SPS 'submitted the month before' is a different instrument from the resiliency plan whose report counted cameras, so a reader can easily merge them.

criteria.name: sequence_and_momentum
criteria.why: The cover's 'Agreed to count fire detections. Counted cameras.' earns the swipe on its own. Frame 2 pays at once with the largest fire in Texas history. The 4 to 5 page swap on the same desk is a real turn, and the reader feels the answer land on the question. Frame 6 makes it physical, and frame 7's 'The cost was counted to the dollar.' is a sharp reversal. Frame 8 is the soft spot. It pulls out to 160 utilities and a pro forma blueprint without saying how either bears on SPS's detections line, and it could be cut without loss. Frame 3 slows the run between the stake and the order. The close asks the right question but lands on filing numbers rather than an act.

criteria.name: voice
criteria.why: It's specific and fair, with no boosterism and no doom. The Panhandle world (caprock, caliche, ranch gate) carries a regional register, and some lines have real snap: 'One line filled. One left bare.' and 'A missing count isn't a count of none.' Other lines sound like a docket clerk. Frame 9's dek, 'The order sits in Docket 57463 and the report SPS filed on May 1st in Project 57941, both on the PUCT Interchange', and frame 2's attribution-led hook 'The Tribune traces the fire to a pole.' both read that way. The caption opens on 'The answer was filed on May 1st.', which gives a feed reader no noun to hold before 'see more'. I found no house-rule breaks (no colons, semicolons, dashes, banned words or first person).

criteria.name: variety
criteria.why: The topic is new to the window (no utility or wildfire deck in topics.json), the stormFront light is new against nos. 32 to 35, and a Panhandle outdoor world is new. The opening move and spine are the ledger's most flagged habit, though. The deck is built on what a document leaves unfilled (the bare rail on frame 6), which decks 11, 14, 15, 16, 23 and 28 each asked the next run to stop leaning on. The instrument, a public body's order read against the regulated party's own filing, is close to the record-against-record reads of nos. 26, 27 and 31. The kit figure-at-a-gate close and the desk-with-a-page document frames are familiar moves from this engine.

one_sentence_fix: Replace frame 8's hearing-room detour with SPS's own August wildfire mitigation plan filing (fetch its docket number and state the 30 day intervention window 16 TAC 25.60(g)(2) gives it, c5, scoped to that case), rendered outdoors in the deck's Panhandle world. The deck would then end on a proceeding a Panhandle reader can actually enter, and the frame whose plate, void and off-topic count cost the most on art, coherence and sequence would be gone.
